# Listing 2.10. The Calculate_Area.java class

```
import org.jsoup.Jsoup;
//Represent an HTML Document.
import org.jsoup.nodes.Document;

public class Calculate_Area extends javax.swing.JFrame {
    /**
     * Auto-generated codes
     */
    private void jButton1ActionPerformed(java.awt.event.ActionEvent evt) {

        try {
            //Define the url to connect to the Java Servlet
            String host = "https://calculatearea.eu-gb.mybluemix.net/?"
                + //parse integer entered in JTextField1
                + "length=" + Integer.parseInt(jTextField1.getText())
                + //parse integer entered in JTextField2
                + "width=" + Integer.parseInt(jTextField2.getText())
            //connect to the URL and fetch the html body
            Document doc = Jsoup.connect(host).ignoreContentType(true).get();
            // Extract the data in text format from URL
            & display the result in jTextField3
            jTextField3.setText(doc.text());
        } catch (Exception ex) {

        }
    }

    /* Auto-generated codes */
```

# 2.8.2. Creating a Mobile Application to Send a Request to the CalculateArea Servlet

This application is developed in the Android Studio IDE by creating a project called CalculateArea. The completed application with a typical output is shown in Figure 2.128. When the SEND PARAMETERS TO CLOUD button is pressed, the values entered in the length and width fields are sent as a URL query to the CalculateArea servlet which responds with the value of the calculated area.
